name: Biren BR100 GPGPU (2-die OAM training accelerator)
memory_bandwidth_basis: PER CHIP, AS PUBLISHED. Biren's Hot Chips 34 presentation states '64GB HBM2E' and the flopper.io spec sheet (citing the same presentation) gives 1.6 TB/s. No direction convention is stated by the vendor. The figure is recorded exactly as published.
notes: THE HIERARCHY POINT: the BR100 is a 2-die 7nm chiplet design on CoWoS packaging with 77 billion transistors, and its compute figures are 2022 launch-release numbers for a part that could not legally be manufactured at TSMC after October 2022 due to US export controls. Treat as historical claims, not shipping specs. HOT CHIPS 34 SPECIFICATIONS (primary vendor source, Mike Hong / Lingjie Xu, August 2022): 'Area 1074mm^2', '2 @7nm', 'TransistorCount 77Billion', 'HostInterface PCIe Gen5 x16 w/CXL', 'PeakPerformance 2048TOPS@INT8, 1024TFLOPS@BF16, 512TFLOPS@TF32+, 256TFLOPS@FP32', 'Memory 64GB HBM2E', 'Interconnections 8 BLink', '2.3TB/s external I/O bandwidth', 'FormFactor OAM with 550W MaxTDP'. CHIPLET DESIGN: 896 GB/s die-to-die interconnect, with the vendor claiming '30% more performance, 20% better yield compared with a monolithic design'. Over 300 MB on-chip SRAM. The presentation carries its own confidentiality legend ('Confidential. This document contains confidential information of BirenTechnology'), so it is a vendor primary source but a weak one to cite for a shipping configuration. Biren was added to the BIS Entity List in October 2023. The BR100 was reportedly modified to process less data so it would fall below the US export threshold. Vendor is 'asic-other' because 'biren' is not in the schema enum.
